class.name: PhysXBuoyancy3D
class.description: Add as a child of a [RigidBody3D] and set [member water_surface_path]. Sample points on the hull each carry a share of the hull's footprint ([member hull_area]): the water pushes each one up by the weight of the water it displaces (density x gravity x area x depth, up to [member hull_height]), so the body settles at its real draft for its mass, pitches and rolls with the waves, and rights itself from the spread of the points. Submerged points drag against the water, and the body disturbs the water's ripple layer, more as it moves. With no [member sample_points], [member hull_area] or [member hull_height] set, they come from the bounds of the body's [CollisionShape3D] children: six points on the bottom (three along the longer side, two across), three quarters of the bounding footprint, and its height. It only applies [RigidBody3D] forces, so it works with whichever physics engine is selected, not just PhysX. For a powered boat, add a [PhysXBoat3D] next to it, and a [PhysXWaterWake3D] for its wake: the body floats on the water without its own wake (other bodies ride it).

method.name: get_effective_sample_points
method.description: The sample points in use, in the body's space: [member sample_points], or the generated ones.

method.name: get_point_depths
method.description: Each sample point's depth below the water surface this physics tick (m); [code]0[/code] or less is above it, [code]-INF[/code] where there is no water.

method.name: get_submerged_fraction
method.description: How much of the hull's buoyancy is in use this physics tick: [code]0[/code] out of the water, [code]1[/code] fully under.

method.name: get_water_height
method.description: The water surface height at [param world_pos] (see [method PhysXWaterSurface3D.sample_height]); [code]-INF[/code] where there is no water.

members.member: Damping on the body's rotation (N·m per rad/s), scaled by how much of the hull is in the water.
Push the water's ripple layer where the body floats, more as it moves.

The hull's footprint on the water (m²), shared between the sample points. With the body's mass it sets the draft: a body floats when [code]water_density * hull_area * depth[/code] equals its mass. [code]0[/code] uses three quarters of the collision shapes' bounding footprint.
How deep (m) the hull can sink before the push stops growing -- the depth at which it is fully under. [code]0[/code] uses the collision shapes' bounding height.

Drag on each submerged point against its velocity (N per m/s per m² of footprint, scaled by how deep it is). Keeps the body from bobbing forever and settles drifting. A [PhysXBoat3D] adds its own directional hull drag on top.
Radius (m) of the body's disturbance in the ripple layer. [code]0[/code] uses half the collision shapes' footprint size.
Speed (m/s) at which the body's disturbance reaches full strength.
Disturbance strength when the body is still ([code]0..1[/code]) -- a small, steady dimple; it ramps up to full strength at [member ripple_reference_speed].

Points on the hull, in the body's space, where the water pushes. Empty generates six on the bottom of the collision shapes' bounds. More points follow the waves more closely; their spread sets how stiffly the body resists pitching and rolling.
Density of the water (kg/m³). [code]1000[/code] for fresh water, about [code]1025[/code] for sea water.
